# Publishing on the Web 🚀

## Why publish?

- The point of an app (or a report) is for **other people** to use it
- Your audience shouldn't need R, RStudio or your laptop
- A link is easy to share: on a résumé, in a portfolio, with a future employer

<br>

For your final project, **both tracks** publish to the web.

## Posit Connect Cloud

- [Posit Connect Cloud](https://connect.posit.cloud/) is Posit's free hosting service for Shiny apps, Quarto documents and more
- It is Posit's successor to shinyapps.io (you may see old tutorials that use shinyapps.io; skip them)
- Free account: sign up with your **GitHub** account
- Your project gets a URL like `https://yourname-project.share.connect.posit.cloud`

## Same steps for apps and reports

<br>

| | Shiny app | Quarto report |
|---|---|---|
| Primary file | `app.R` | `report.qmd` |
| Content type to pick | **Shiny** | **Quarto** |
| Everything else | same | same |

<br>

Example: [FRED app](https://eteitelbaum-fred-app.share.connect.posit.cloud/)

## Two ways to publish

<br>

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**1. From your IDE**

- Click the **Publish** button in RStudio
- Or use **Posit Publisher** in Positron
- Quickest way to get started
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**2. From GitHub**

- Push your project to a public GitHub repo
- Publish from the Connect Cloud website
- Updates automatically every time you push
:::
:::

# Before You Publish ✅

## Get your project folder in order

- Everything the project needs lives **in one folder**: `app.R` or `report.qmd`, data files, helper scripts
- Use **relative paths**: `read_csv("data/my_data.csv")`, not `"/Users/me/Desktop/..."`
- No `setwd()` and no `install.packages()` in your code
- Load every package with `library()` at the top so Connect Cloud knows what to install
- Run it one more time on your own machine, from a fresh R session

## Don't publish your API keys! 🔑

- On the free plan, the GitHub route requires a **public** repo---anyone can read your code
- **Option 1:** download the data once, save it to a `.csv` or `.rds`, and publish the file
- **Option 2:** store the key as a **secret variable** in Connect Cloud and read it with `Sys.getenv()`

```{r}
#| label: secret
fredr_set_key(Sys.getenv("FRED_API_KEY"))
```

- Locally, put `FRED_API_KEY=yourkey` in an `.Renviron` file (and never commit it)

# Route 1: From Your IDE 🖱️

## Publishing from RStudio

1. Open your `app.R` (or render your `report.qmd`)
2. Click the blue **Publish** icon at the top of the editor
3. Choose **Posit Connect Cloud** and log in to connect your account (first time only)
4. Select the files to upload: your main file plus data and helper scripts
5. Click **Publish**

<br>

To update: save your changes and click **Publish** again.

## Publishing from Positron

1. Click the **Posit Publisher** icon in the Activity Bar
2. Under **Credentials**, click **+** and choose **Posit Connect Cloud**; authorize in the browser
3. Add a deployment and pick your `app.R` or `report.qmd`
4. Confirm the project files and add any **secrets** (e.g., API keys)
5. Click **Deploy Your Project**

<br>

Positron needs an `renv.lock` file for R projects: run `renv::init()` first.

# Route 2: From GitHub 🐙

## Create a manifest

Connect Cloud needs to know which packages (and versions) your project uses. From the folder with your main file, run:

```{r}
#| label: manifest
# install.packages("rsconnect")
rsconnect::writeManifest()
```

<br>

This creates a `manifest.json` file. Re-run it whenever you add a package.

## Push and publish

1. Commit your main file, `manifest.json` and any data or helper files and **push** to a public GitHub repo
2. Sign in to [Connect Cloud](https://connect.posit.cloud/) and click **Publish**
3. Install the **GitHub App** when prompted (first time only)
4. Choose **Shiny** or **Quarto**, then your repo and branch (`main`)
5. Set the **primary file** (`app.R` or `report.qmd`)
6. Under **Advanced settings**, add any secret variables
7. Click **Publish**

## Updating your project

- With **automatic publishing** on, every push to `main` republishes
- Otherwise, click **Republish** on the content page
- Check the **logs** on the content page if something goes wrong

# Authoring a Report in Quarto 📝

## Start with the YAML header

```{.yaml}
---
title: "Democracy and Development, 1990-2024"
author: "Your Name(s)"
date: today
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    embed-resources: true
execute:
  echo: false
  message: false
  warning: false
---
```

- `echo: false` hides your code so the report reads like a finished piece
- `embed-resources: true` packs images and styles into a single HTML file

## Structure with headings

```{.markdown}
## Introduction

What question are you asking, and why does it matter?

## Data

Where do the data come from? What do the key variables measure?

## Findings

Walk the reader through your visualizations.

## Conclusion

What did we learn? What are the limits?
```

## Label, caption and cross-reference figures

```{.r}
#| label: fig-trend
#| fig-cap: "Average electoral democracy score by region, 1990-2024. Source: V-Dem."

ggplot(dem_data, aes(x = year, y = polyarchy, color = region)) +
  geom_line()
```

<br>

Then point to it in your text:

```{.markdown}
As @fig-trend shows, democracy declined in most regions after 2010.
```

## Writing tips

- **Lead with the takeaway:** tell the reader what to notice before (or right after) the figure
- One idea per paragraph; one main point per figure
- Use callouts (`::: {.callout-note}`) for definitions or caveats
- Render early and often: problems are easier to fix one at a time

<br>

More: [Quarto guide](https://quarto.org/docs/guide/) and our [Quarto and Markdown](/modules/getting-started-2.qmd) module.

# Troubleshooting 🔧

## Common problems

- **"There is no package called..."**: you forgot a `library()` call, or need to re-run `writeManifest()`
- **"Cannot open file..."**: an absolute path, or you didn't upload the data file
- **App works locally, fails online:** check the logs on the content page
- **Blank chart or error from an API:** your key isn't set on Connect Cloud
- Always open your published link in a **private browser window** to see what others see
